## 🚀 Lium Backend API

A comprehensive compute platform that enables users to rent GPU resources from a network of providers/nodes.


*Built with FastAPI, PostgreSQL and Redis.*

post.summary: Rent the cheapest node matching a spec
post.description: Rent one node without naming it: the server picks the cheapest rentable node ($/GPU·h) that satisfies every constraint in the request and rents it in the same call. Ties go to the faster ingress, then the higher reliability score (a node without a score ranks at the median score of the matching nodes), then the node id, so the same catalogue always yields the same pick. If the pick is taken between selection and rent the next candidate is tried (up to 3 in all); `attempts` says how many it took. With `dry_run=true` nothing is rented: the response carries the pick, its price and the template that would be used, so a client can show them before asking to confirm. When no node satisfies the spec the response is 409 `no_executor_matches_spec` naming the first constraint that left no candidate and the best value the remaining nodes offered for it. Everything else (authentication, balance, template, SSH keys, ports) behaves exactly as `POST /executors/{executor_uuid}/rent`, the `Idempotency-Key` header included: a retry with the same key and body returns the first call's pod instead of renting another node.

post.description: Endpoint to rent a node with the provided details. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1-255 letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`, `:`; a UUID is fine) to make a retry safe: within 24 h the same key with the byte-identical body returns the first call's answer (the same `pod_id`) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and `Idempotency-Original-Request-Id`; a refused rent (4xx) is replayed the same way, and the same key with a corrected body runs again. Without the header every call rents.

get.description: Everything the account was charged for this pod, read from the billing ledger rather than the pod row, so it answers for a removed pod as well as a running one. `total` is the sum of the pod's ledger rows; `days` lists those rows oldest first (a UTC day can have more than one, for example when billing stops and resumes) with the seconds and $/h behind each amount; for a removed pod the last row carries the final settlement made on removal and `removed_at`/`close_reason` say when and why it ended. post.summary: Top up the balance from a saved card, without a browser
post.description: Charges `amount_usd` to the saved default card (or `payment_method_id`) off-session and records the pending top-up; the balance is credited by the Stripe webhook, as after a Checkout. Risk checks decide whether the charge goes off-session or steps up to a 3-D Secure challenge; a step-up, or a bank that asks for authentication, answers 402 `CARD_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` with `next_action_url`: the cardholder confirms there and the webhook credits the balance, with no further call (a repeat with the same key answers the same URL). Through a key with a spending budget, a previously verified card normally charges without another confirmation. Lium asks again if it cannot confirm the earlier check, and the bank can always require confirmation. Other callers also step up past the 24-hour velocity. A step-up is authorized only and captured only when its 3-D Secure result shifted the fraud liability to the bank; otherwise the authorization is canceled and the call refused with 402 `CARD_AUTHENTICATION_UNAVAILABLE`, charged nothing. A wallet (Link, Apple Pay, Google Pay) is refused with 402 `WALLET_NOT_SUPPORTED` before anything is written or sent to the bank. A 402 without `next_action_url`, or `CARD_DECLINED`, is final: retry with a new `idempotency_key` (the same key always replays it and cannot charge twice). 202 `processing`: the row is not credited yet (first call or a repeat), or Stripe's answer to the charge call was lost. 200 `succeeded` only once the row is COMPLETED (credited by the webhook, or by this call when it captured a confirmed step-up). First and repeat read that same row, so a succeeded PaymentIntent stays `processing` until the credit. Do not repeat the call without the returned `idempotency_key`; with it the repeat is the same transaction. The same key with a different amount is a new charge. DiskHealthSpec.title: DiskHealthSpec
DiskHealthSpec.description:
DAH-2929: the validator's disk probe (lium-io DAH-2928, lium-io#1278), one cycle's readings.

lium-io#1278 (15 Sep, value audit) sends four keys: ``docker_root_dir``, ``read_only_mounts``,
``write_probe`` and ``write_probe_error``. Each is what the scrape measured that cycle; None or
empty where it could not. The dmesg, sysfs, NVMe and SMART readers were cut from the probe before

here in the same change.

CONTRACT OBLIGATION (same as GpuMetrics): MachineSpecs validates with Pydantic's default
``extra="ignore"``, so a probe key the validator starts emitting that is not declared here is
stripped on the upsert, not stored. Declare it here to keep it.

``BillingHistoryForMinerResponse`` serialize specs through ``public_specs_projection``;
``ExecutorForProviderResponse`` declares the same two fields in ``PublicDiskHealth``, DAH-3462): the
free-text readings (docker root path, exception text) stay in the
stored specs for operators. The machine request owner's ``GET /machine-requests/{id}/executors`` serves the
row's address fields (DAH-2554: ip, ssh port, coldkey by design) and the projected specs (DAH-4180).

GpuActivitySpec.title: GpuActivitySpec

One GPU's load at scrape time next to whether a rental held it — a rule input, not a verdict.

Derived by the backend on every validator report (`services/gpu_activity.py`, called from
`worker.save_executor_into_db`), never sent by the validator. `util_pct` and `vram_used_mb` are
`gpu.details[].gpu_utilization` / `memory_used_mb` of the same report; `no_pod` is "no
`executor_gpu` row with this `uuid` has a `pod_id`" at save time — the backend's own record of
which GPU a rental holds, which the scrape cannot see (its `gpu_processes` is read from inside
the executor container, so a process on the host is invisible to it: rel-box-34 case 11, executor
252f0496, 14-100 % utilisation for hours with no pod and `gpu_processes` `[]` in 672/672 snapshots).

`no_pod` says nothing about a default job (filler): a filler holds no `executor_gpu.pod_id`, so a
GPU it uses reads `no_pod: true` with load. A consumer excludes fillers through
`specs.docker.containers` (`filler_` prefix), as the loop's host-load detector already does.

documented way to surface it; failing to do so is a silent-strip data-loss bug, not a
crash.

what he can actually put in a cart. Renting is still per node: nothing here reserves the group.

InfinibandPortSpec.title: InfinibandPortSpec
InfinibandPortSpec.description:
One RDMA port as the executor's kernel reports it (DAH-2571).

`link_layer` is the ONLY safe way to tell InfiniBand from RoCE: mlx5 reports `lid` 0x0 on an
Ethernet port but Intel irdma reports 0x1, measured on prod 2026-08-05.

What identifies a fabric: on InfiniBand, `sm_lid` with the LID set — a host running its own
subnet manager reports `sm_lid` 0x1 pointing at its own port, so it is a one-host subnet, while
an external switch-side SM shows up as something else (0xe on the one real multi-node fabric in
the fleet). On RoCE it is the IPv4-mapped entry of `gids` — find it by the
`0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:ffff:` prefix, never by index: mlx5 puts it at 2-3, Intel irdma at 1.
The GID prefix is NOT usable — every prod port carries the default `fe80::`.

Those IPv4-mapped addresses are private (172.16/10.x observed on prod), so they identify a
segment only WITHIN one provider — two providers can hand out the same one. Pair on them only
together with something provider-scoped.

`rate` is meaningful only while `state` is ACTIVE; on a DOWN port the driver fills in a
placeholder rather than the card's real capability.

InterconnectSpec.title: InterconnectSpec
InterconnectSpec.description:
How the GPUs of one host are wired to each other, from the validator's `nvidia-smi topo` run.

Scraped by lium-io DAH-2922, declared and exposed here (DAH-2923).
`nvlink` is True only when EVERY GPU pair is joined by NVLink (an HGX board); a box with NVLink
bridges on some pairs reports False with `nvlink_pairs` < `gpu_pairs`. `p2p` is True only when
every pair of `nvidia-smi topo -p2p r` reads OK — False is the host where NCCL cannot start
without NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1. Both are None on a single-GPU host (nothing to judge) and when the
table that answers them could not be read (`interconnect_scrape_error` on MachineSpecs says why).
`pcie_class` is nvidia-smi's worst class among the non-NVLink pairs (SYS > NODE > PHB > PXB > PIX).
`matrix` is the GPU x GPU cell table, kept so a client can print the topology.

Null on non-failed restores, on restores failed before this field existed, and on the legacy engine.

failed_at.title: Failed At
failed_at.description: When the restore was marked FAILED (UTC).

RoceLinkMeasurementSpec.title: RoceLinkMeasurementSpec
RoceLinkMeasurementSpec.description:
What the validator measured between this host and ONE neighbour on its segment (DAH-2667).

A RoCE fabric is otherwise only inferred from addresses, and a shared segment is not proof that
the switch carries RDMA. The validator runs `ib_write_bw` between the free hosts of a segment
and writes one of these per pair into the specs of BOTH hosts, each naming the other.

`gigabits_per_second` is None when that pair could not talk — a recorded failure, not silence.

ScheduledNoticeResponse.title: ScheduledNoticeResponse
ScheduledNoticeResponse.description:
A provider's open maintenance or removal notice on a listed node, shown before the renter rents it.

When `expiring_at` passes, `handle_notice_period` reboots a pod on the node (maintenance) or deletes it
(`permanent_removal`), so a rental taken now is interrupted then. The provider's free-text reason is left out.
